evidence.claim: From Highway 70 east of Eagle River, the approach to Franklin Lake turns south onto Military Road, then east onto Butternut Lake Road.
evidence.quote: From Eagle River: Travel east 7.6 miles on Highway 70 to FR 2178 (Military Road). Turn right (south) on FR 2178 and continue 2.8 miles to FR 2181 (Butternut Lake Road). Turn left (east) and travel 4.6 miles to the campground.

evidence.claim: At the lake, historic stone and log buildings stand among mature pines and hemlocks.
evidence.quote: The campground is situated in a lush stand of mature pine and hemlock trees, at an elevation of 1,700 feet. Historic stone and log structures, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, are scattered throughout the campground.

evidence.claim: The Franklin Nature Trail continues through forest to a view of Butternut Lake and a boardwalk across a bog.
evidence.quote: The trail will lead you through northern hardwood, pine, and hemlock forests where some trees are over 400 years old. You can stop off at Butternut Lake and view the beautiful lake from under huge hemlock trees. The boardwalk across the bog offers a chance to see many varieties of bog plants up close.
